title: Say what reads a role's model, stop the colour test passing on a near-miss, and name the rule the publish and close gates share

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 45, round 1. Audited commit 0426b01 (on 3c2c2a9, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD and is unchanged since 3c2c2a9. Verdict: PASS.

1. Req 1: one statement beside the team table, naming both routes, and I checked both claims against run-role.js rather than taking the sentence on trust (the criterion says to):
 - Headless: headlessLaunchArgs builds `const definition = { description, prompt }` and then `if (meta && meta.model) definition.model = meta.model;` before `JSON.stringify({ [role.id]: definition })`. So the model genuinely is passed in the --agents JSON, as claimed.
 - Interactive: freshLaunchArgs returns ['--agent', role.id, '--session-id', uuid, '--name', sessionTitle, prompt] and resumeLaunchArgs ['--agent', role.id, '--resume', uuid, ...]. Neither passes --model, and a grep for a --model argv anywhere in run-role.js/prompts.js finds none. So "this framework's own launcher never passes a --model flag on this path at all" is exactly true.
 - The frontmatter-beats---model claim is attributed to sprint 12's measurement rather than re-asserted as new, which is the right provenance.
 - It is one statement in the table's own section, not six scattered comments.
2. Req 2: the stale "e.g. `claude --model opus`" example is gone (0 occurrences). What replaces it tells an operator to launch with `claude --agent <id>`, says the agent file is pasted in and the declared model already applies, and explicitly warns that passing --model would describe something with no effect. Consistent with Req 1 and it does not imply the flag sets the model.
3. Req 3: QA1 planted both cases the criterion names, each reverted after:
 - Look-alike pair: dev-team-2 back to `orange` (terminal.ansiBrightYellow) against QA1's `yellow` (terminal.ansiYellow) -- the exact defect that reached the operator, and the case that PASSED in sprint 44. It now FAILS by name: "no two role task colors form a known look-alike pair, not just an exact collision (sprint 45, Req 3)". That closes the gap I recorded in sprint 44.
 - Genuinely distinct colours: swapping dev-team-2 and liveqa (purple/cyan) PASSES, so the new check does not fire on any legitimate change.
 - Worth recording honestly: my first attempt at the distinct-colour plant used `green`, which pipeman already declares, so it created a real exact collision and correctly failed sprint 44's distinctness test. That was my planting error, not a defect; I redid it with a valid swap rather than counting the first run.
 - The exact-duplicate property from sprint 44 still holds (dev-team-2 to `yellow` still fails).
 - 3a: the comment states plainly that look-alike-ness is theme- and eyesight-dependent, cannot be measured in a unit test, and that the list is deliberately conservative rather than a claim about every theme. Extending it to every base/bright ANSI pair is sound: it is the same failure mode by construction, and it costs nothing since the map only uses one bright variant today.
 - 3b: the comment says the list is not a substitute for a person looking at rendered tabs, names sprint 44's screenshot as the real coverage for unlisted pairs, and frames a future report as new evidence to add rather than as proof the test should already have caught it.
4. Req 4: the paragraph states the principle generally, names all three instances (a sprint closing, a release publishing, a role's model changing on an unattended upgrade), credits FMC's Master Controller with the date, and says which two have gates and which deliberately does not. The framing is a reason gates exist, not licence to skip one -- it ends by telling whoever designs the next gate to ask the question deliberately.
 - 4a: no gate and no behaviour change. scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py and scripts/launcher/ have a zero-line diff across the whole sprint; the only files touched are CLAUDE.md, scripts/launcher_test.js, package.json and CHANGELOG.md, which is exactly the declared scope.
5. Req 5: npm view fully-completely version returns 0.2.19 and package.json is 0.2.20, published+1 confirmed at build time, with a CHANGELOG entry covering Reqs 1-4.
6. Req 6: both suites at 0426b01 in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0.

FOR LIVEQA. The sprint's criteria are the right set. One emphasis: Req 1's live check is the one that matters most here, because a statement about what reads `model:` is exactly the kind of claim that can be true when written and false after a refactor. Take the model from the structured envelope on both paths (interactive and headless) as sprint 44 established, and if either path stops honouring frontmatter, that is a break in the property this sprint documents, not drift.

FAIL: LiveQA live test, sprint 45, round 1. Verdict: FAIL.
One confirmed defect, in the requirement this sprint exists to deliver: CLAUDE.md states, as a measured fact, that an agent file's frontmatter beats an explicit --model flag. At the CLI version current at gate time it does not — the flag wins. Two passages are affected, and one of them tells operators the flag has no effect, which is actively misleading. Everything else in the sprint passed; detail below, so one fix round covers it all.

ENVIRONMENT
macOS 26.6.2 arm64, node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, git 2.55.0. **Claude Code CLI 2.1.280 at gate time.** 2026-09-23. Scratch install s45/proj (a real npx install of the published 0.2.20) and a clean clone at 0426b01 for the test suite. Evidence for every model result is the structured `modelUsage` key of each run's own JSON envelope, never the model's narration.

PROVENANCE (registry, not the handoff)
npm dist-tags latest 0.2.20. npm view fully-completely@0.2.20 gitHead 0426b018ee192cde6da79d818fe77dade876f998 == last_shipped_commit. dist.shasum b34ec2e14793040bea03eccd9e9e1fd66272d37e == the npm pack download. All 59 published files byte-identical to git show 0426b01:<path> (MISMATCHED 0, NOT-IN-COMMIT 0).

THE DEFECT (Req 1, and Req 2's rewrite which repeats it)

The shipped CLAUDE.md says, beside the team table:
  "An interactive launch (`claude --agent <id>`) has the CLI itself read that role's own agent-file frontmatter directly — this framework's own launcher never passes a `--model` flag on this path at all, and frontmatter wins even when one is given anyway (measured: `--agent <id> --model haiku` still ran as `<id>`'s own frontmatter model, not haiku)."
And, in the run-each-role paragraph Req 2 rewrote:
  "never pass `--model` yourself to select it, the flag exists but does not override the agent file's own frontmatter (see the paragraph just above), so naming a value there would describe something with no effect."

Measured at claude 2.1.280, in the installed 0.2.20 scratch project, 2 reps each, identical both times:
  claude --agent qa1                      -> modelUsage ['claude-opus-5-5']        (frontmatter opus)
  claude --agent qa1 --model haiku        -> modelUsage ['claude-haiku-4-5-20251001']
  claude --agent qa1 --model sonnet       -> modelUsage ['claude-sonnet-5']
  claude --agent pipeman                  -> modelUsage ['claude-sonnet-5']        (frontmatter sonnet)
  claude --agent pipeman --model opus     -> modelUsage ['claude-opus-5-5']
  claude --agent dev-team-1 --model haiku -> modelUsage ['claude-haiku-4-5-20251001']
  claude --model haiku (no --agent)       -> modelUsage ['claude-haiku-4-5-20251001']   (control: the flag works on its own)
So the flag overrides frontmatter in every case tried, in both directions (a weaker model over opus, a stronger model over sonnet), for three different model values. The parenthetical "measured" claim is false at this CLI version, and the guidance sentence is worse than false: an operator who reads "describes something with no effect" and passes --model anyway silently changes the model of a role, which is exactly the cost-by-default the sprint's own Req 4 paragraph warns about.

This is the sprint's own live criterion firing as written: "Confirm Req 1's claim is still true rather than merely present ... A statement about what reads `model:` that has quietly stopped being true is worse than no statement."

Grade: CONFIRMED (2/2 reps, three model values, both directions, structured envelope plus an independent control). Not model-mediated narration.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG — the core of Req 1 holds
The two routes themselves are honoured, which is the substantive half of the requirement:
- Interactive, no flag: `claude --agent qa1` ran opus-5-5 and `claude --agent pipeman` ran sonnet-5 — the CLI does read the agent file's frontmatter.
- Headless, via run-role.js's `--agents` JSON: pipeman -> claude-sonnet-5, liveqa -> claude-opus-5-5.
So `model:` is a real control on both paths. Only the claim about flag precedence has gone stale.

EVERYTHING ELSE PASSED
- Req 4a, checked first: git diff 3cc6b90..0426b01 over scripts/launcher/, scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py, scripts/install.js, scripts/gate-commit.js and scripts/mc-commit.js is ZERO lines. No gate, no behaviour change.
- Req 2's stale example is gone: no "e.g. `claude --model opus` for Master Controller, QA1, or LiveQA" remains. What replaces it is consistent with Req 1 — and shares its one false claim, above.
- Req 4: the principle paragraph is present at CLAUDE.md line 60, "Taking a cost by default is not the same as choosing it (sprint 45, credited to FMC's Master Controller, 22 September)", naming a sprint closing, a release publishing, and a role's model changing under an unattended upgrade as the three instances.
- Table vs frontmatter, all six roles, read from the install: master-controller opus/opus, dev-team-1 opus/opus, dev-team-2 opus/opus, qa1 opus/opus, pipeman sonnet/sonnet, liveqa opus/opus. ALL MATCH.
- Req 3: LOOK_ALIKE_COLOR_PAIRS exists in scripts/launcher_test.js with all eight colour/bright-variant pairs, yellow/bright-yellow marked "the confirmed pair -- sprint 44's own defect", and a test asserting no two role colours form a listed pair. The comment above it states the judgment and its bounds (3a) and that a rendered human check remains the only coverage for an unlisted pair (3b). `node scripts/launcher_test.js` at 0426b01 in a clean clone: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED.

A NOTE ON ONE CRITERION AS WRITTEN
The live criterion says to "confirm the suite is present in the install and passes there". It is not present in an install: scripts/launcher_test.js is not in the package manifest, and never has been (the same is true of the findings docs — sprint 22 recorded what the package ships). I ran it from a clean clone at the shipped commit instead, which is the same code. Not a defect, but the criterion should say so next time rather than sending the next LiveQA looking for a file that is deliberately not shipped.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS
Documentation only; no code is implicated.
1. Correct both passages. The honest statement at claude 2.1.280 is: this framework's launcher never passes --model on the interactive path, so a role launched the documented way runs on its frontmatter model; an explicit --model DOES override frontmatter, so do not pass one unless you intend to change the model for that session.
2. Anchor the claim to a CLI version, as this project does elsewhere — sprint 12's measurement was true when made; the CLI has moved (2.1.261 -> 2.1.272 -> 2.1.278 -> 2.1.280 across this epic alone), and an unanchored "measured" parenthetical is what let a stale fact ship as current.
3. Consider a test: this property is measurable in a launched session (the modelUsage envelope), so it need not rely on prose. That is a Master Controller call, not a LiveQA requirement.
Retest scope for the next round is narrow: re-read the two passages, re-run the six flag/no-flag cases above at whatever CLI is current, and redo provenance on the new gitHead. Nothing else needs repeating.
